summary.text: Fish migration is the mass movement of fish from one area or body of water to another, over distances from a few metres to thousands of kilometres.
Fish usually migrate to feed better or to reproduce, though in some cases the reasons are unclear.
Anadromous fish such as salmon live in the sea and spawn in fresh water, while catadromous fish such as freshwater eels do the reverse.

items.prompt: Freshwater eels live their adult lives in rivers but travel to salt water to breed. What is that pattern called?
items.explain: Catadromous fish live in fresh water as adults and migrate into salt water to spawn; anadromous fish do the opposite.

items.prompt: Herring spend feeding time far from the waters where their young grow up. What problem might this help avoid?

options.label: Young fish eating all the plankton adults need
Adults and young being caught in the same net
Parasites passing from adults to the young
Adults eating their own young, which they cannot recognise

items.explain: Forage fish cannot identify their own offspring, so wide triangular journeys between spawning, feeding and nursery grounds may prevent cannibalism.

items.prompt: Fishers notice tuna appear farther north as the season warms and vanish in cooler months. What are the tuna following?
items.explain: Some fish such as tuna move north and south at different times of year following temperature gradients.

items.prompt: Many sea fish are found near the surface after dark but in deeper layers by day. What is this daily pattern called?
items.explain: Many marine fish make a diel vertical migration, rising to the surface to feed at night and sinking to lower layers by day.

items.prompt: Why does the law of the sea treat tuna and marlin differently from most fish?

options.label: They roam in and out of waters that different nations control
They breed in rivers that cross national borders
They are farmed in ocean cages that no nation owns
They live on the sea floor beyond any country's waters

items.explain: Highly migratory species are large pelagic fish that move in and out of the exclusive economic zones of different nations, and the treaty covers them separately.

items.prompt: A forecaster wants to predict where Icelandic capelin will travel. Which factor shapes their migration?

options.label: The salt level of the water

items.explain: The capelin migration is affected by ocean currents, and a particle model has predicted the spawning route.
